strategy.bottleneck: [compute-bound tensor-core mainloop] The two cuDNN `sm90_xmma_fprop_implicit_gemm_f32f32_tf32f32_f32_nhwckrsc_nhwc_tilesize64x128x32` convolutions (2 launches/forward) consume ~804us of the 1179us forward — all five profiled custom kernels sum to only 375us. The convs run 1.546e11 FLOP at ~192 TFLOP/s, ~51% of TF32 dense peak, i.e. a sub-optimal cuDNN engine-config chosen by heuristics.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: vendor_algo_autotune: keep the cuDNN implicit-GEMM mainloop (default-keep rule) but replace heuristic plan selection with cuDNN exhaustive benchmark selection for our two conv calls only (locally toggled inside the extension, restored afterwards so the reference path is untouched). Metrics show the conv segment is 68% of runtime at ~51% of TF32 peak while every custom kernel is already at 73–82% of DRAM peak; engine-config/tile/split-K choice is the only sanctioned lever with >5% expected gain.
strategy.modification_plan:
1. EXACT CODE ACTION (enable exhaustive cuDNN plan search, scoped): in `fused_res_block`, immediately after the input checks add an RAII guard:
   `struct BmGuard { bool prev; BmGuard():prev(at::globalContext().benchmarkCuDNN()){ at::globalContext().setBenchmarkCuDNN(true);} ~BmGuard(){ at::globalContext().setBenchmarkCuDNN(prev);} } _bm;`
   This makes both `at::conv2d` calls take PyTorch's cuDNN-v8 `try_all` path (times every engine config, caches the winner per shape/layout key) and restores the previous flag on return so the eager reference `F.conv2d` timing and global state are unchanged.
2. EXACT CODE ACTION (keep numerics identical): right below the guard add `at::globalContext().setAllowTF32CuDNN(true);` (restore the previous value in the same guard). This keeps the same TF32 arithmetic the reference uses, so the exhaustive search only reorders tiles/split-K, never precision. Leave the two `at::conv2d(xl, w1c, nobias, {1,1}, {1,1})` / `(y1s, w2c, ...)` call sites textually unchanged — no layout, no dtype, no bias changes.
3. Alternative call form (only if the installed ATen exposes it; keep flag route as default because it is API-version-safe): `at::cudnn_convolution(xl, w1c, /*padding*/{1,1}, /*stride*/{1,1}, /*dilation*/{1,1}, /*groups*/1, /*benchmark*/true, /*deterministic*/false, /*allow_tf32*/true)`. Do not mix both forms.
4. Do NOT touch K1..K5 this round (nchw2nhwc, stats_partial, stats_finalize, gn_silu_nhwc, gn_silu_res_nchw) — they are already at 72.8–82.3% of DRAM peak, so they are outside the single-method scope.
5. Cache-warm behaviour: the plan search runs once per distinct (N,C,H,W,layout) key. The harness executes warmup iterations before timing, so 4 shapes x 2 convs = 8 searches are amortised. Keep the guard unconditional (no shape gating) so the small 2x256x64x64 shape also gets its cached winner; a cache hit is a hash lookup (<1us).
6. Keep the existing `!y.is_contiguous(ChannelsLast)` re-contiguify checks: an autotuned engine could in principle emit a differently-strided output; the guard keeps correctness and, when the output is already channels-last, costs nothing.
7. Validation checklist: (a) run nsys and confirm the fprop kernel name/tile changed (expect e.g. `tilesize128x128x32` or a split-K variant) and its duration dropped; (b) re-check max|out-ref| on all four shapes against the per-workload tolerances (0.0027–0.003 atol) — TF32 stays enabled so error should be unchanged; (c) confirm the flag is restored by asserting `torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark` is unchanged after a forward.
8. Anti-regression gate: score all four shapes; accept only if the geometric mean improves and no individual shape regresses by more than 2%. If the awkward 1x256x131x131 shape regresses (odd extents can make some engines pad heavily), keep the guard but wrap it in `if (P >= 4096)`; otherwise leave it unconditional.
9. Roll-back criterion: if the chosen engine is identical on all four shapes (no kernel-name change in nsys) and total time moves <1%, revert the guard and, in the NEXT round (separate method), target `gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel` with float4 tile transpose to lift its 72.77% DRAM utilisation toward the 82% its siblings reach.

Conv work = 2 x 2*8*256*256*9*8192 = 1.546e11 FLOP -> ~192 TFLOP/s, ~51% of TF32 dense peak: heuristic engine-config leaves ~1.9x headroom on the dominant segment. Refutation of the 'memory-bound epilogue' alternative: nchw2nhwc is at 80.93% and gn_silu_nhwc at 82.29% of DRAM peak (already saturated); even lifting the worst, gn_silu_res_nchw (72.77%, 128.8us), to 82% saves only ~13us = 1.1% of the forward — an order of magnitude less than the conv lever.

(2) End-to-end mid-shape speedup 1.39x -> >=1.50x; geometric mean over the 4 shapes up. (3) DRAM throughput of K1/K4/K5 must stay at 72-83% (unchanged) and launch count stays 11/forward. strategy.bottleneck: [memory/DRAM-bound, cold-L2 re-read] The five custom kernels move 603 MB/forward at ~80% DRAM; the hottest, gn_silu_res_nchw (129.9 us) plus stats_partial (2x42.7 us) exist only to re-read intermediates the previous kernel just wrote. Working set (67 MB/tensor) exceeds the 50 MB L2, so every re-read (stats1, K4, conv2 input, stats2, K5) is a full DRAM round trip.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Cache-blocking the whole fused block over the batch axis so each chunk's intermediates stay L2-resident: run K1 -> conv1 -> stats -> K4 -> conv2 -> stats -> K5 on 1-2 samples at a time, reusing the same temp buffers. GroupNorm statistics are per (n, group) and the residual is elementwise, so batch chunking is exactly equivalent. Evidence: stats_partial lts__t_sector_hit_rate = 4.31% (L2 hit 5.33%) while re-reading a tensor written by the immediately preceding conv; converting those re-reads to L2 hits removes up to 335 MB of DRAM traffic.
strategy.modification_plan:
1) In fused_res_block, after computing N,C,H,W,P, add exact code: `const size_t bps = (size_t)C*P*4; const size_t BUDGET = 16ull<<20; int chunkN = (int)(BUDGET / (bps>0?bps:1)); if (chunkN < 1) chunkN = 1; if (chunkN > N) chunkN = N;` then `const bool chunked = (N > chunkN);`. If !chunked, execute exactly today's code path (bit-identical for N=1 and for the 2x256x64x64 shape, where bps=4.2MB -> chunkN>=N).
2) If chunked, hoist ALL allocations and the two weight conversions out of the loop, then loop the whole pipeline: allocate once `xl, y1s` (channels_last) and `out` (NCHW) for the FULL N (out must be full-size); allocate `w1c=w1.contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, `w2c` once before the loop. Then `for (int n0=0; n0<N; n0+=chunkN){ int nb=min(chunkN,N-n0); ... }` where inside the body every kernel launch uses grid.z/gridDim.y = nb and base pointers offset by `(size_t)n0*C*P`:
   - K1: `nchw2nhwc_kernel<<<dim3((P+31)/32, C/32, nb)>>>(xptr + n0*C*P, xlptr + n0*C*P, P, C)`.
   - conv1: build chunk views with `xl.narrow(0,n0,nb)` (batch-major slice is contiguous in both NCHW and NHWC, no copy) and call `at::conv2d(xl_chunk, w1c, nobias, {1,1},{1,1})` -> y1_chunk (fresh 16 MB alloc, reused by the caching allocator across chunks, which also maximises L2 address reuse).
   - compute_scale_shift(y1_chunk.data_ptr, nb, C, P, G, g1,b1,...): pass nb as N so the partial buffer, nchunks cap and grid.y all shrink; the buffer is allocated inside that helper per chunk (small).
   - K4 gn_silu_nhwc: grid.y = nb, pointers offset for y1s by n0*C*P.
   - conv2 on y1s.narrow(0,n0,nb) -> y2_chunk; compute_scale_shift with nb.
   - K5 gn_silu_res_nchw: `<<<dim3((P+31)/32, C/32, nb)>>>(y2ptr, xptr + n0*C*P, outptr + n0*C*P, sc2, sh2, P, C)`.
3) Keep everything on `at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()` and strictly sequential (single stream) — the L2 win depends on temporal locality, so do NOT add extra streams or overlap.
4) Do not change any kernel body, block size, dtype, or the TF32 conv path; only grid.z/gridDim.y and base pointers vary. The scale/shift tensors are per-chunk of shape {nb,C}, and gn_silu_nhwc indexes them by blockIdx.y in [0,nb), which already matches.
5) Correctness guards: assert nb>=1; tail chunk (nb<chunkN) is handled because every kernel derives its extent from nb, and stats_partial always writes its partial slot (no unwritten tail). P is never tiled, so the 131x131 (odd P) shape is untouched (N=1 -> unchunked path).
6) Tune BUDGET: try 16 MB (mid shape -> chunkN=2, 4 chunks); if the mid shape does not improve, retry 24 MB (chunkN=3). Cap the number of chunks at 8 to bound launch overhead (`if (N/chunkN > 8) chunkN = (N+7)/8;`).
7) Verify launch counts: unchunked shapes stay at 7 kernels + 2 convs; mid shape becomes <= 4x that, all async on one stream.
strategy.evidence: stats_partial_kernel: lts__t_sector_hit_rate = 4.31% (section L2 Hit Rate 5.33%), l1tex hit 0%, DRAM 79.9%, 42.7 us x2 — it re-reads the 67 MB conv output written one kernel earlier, and 67 MB > 50 MB L2, so every sector misses. gn_silu_res_nchw L2 hit 33.3% for the same reason. Root cause: the working set per stage (67 MB) exceeds L2, so five separate re-reads (stats1, K4, conv2 input, stats2, K5) each cost full DRAM bandwidth (~335 MB of the 871 MB/forward). Refutation of the alternative 'K5 is un-vectorized/smem-transpose bound': K5 moves 201 MB, whose roofline at the measured ~2.03 TB/s is 99 us vs 129.9 us measured — only ~30 us (2.5% of the 1179 us forward) of slack, an order of magnitude less than the 335 MB of removable re-read traffic.

strategy.bottleneck: [memory/DRAM-bound, low-width access] Hottest modifiable kernel is gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel (129.2 us/launch, 34% of the 375 us custom-kernel budget). It moves 201 MB (y2 NHWC read + x NCHW read + NCHW write) yet reaches only 72.5% DRAM vs 81-82% for the sibling streaming kernels: every access is a scalar 4-byte load/store (32 threads = 128 B/request), so 4x more memory instructions per byte and too little memory-level parallelism. The cuDNN convs are default-keep vendor mainloops (already algo-autotuned in round 1).
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: mem_vectorize: rewrite the shared-memory tile transpose in gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel (and the identical pattern in nchw2nhwc_kernel) so every global access is a float4. NHWC side reads 4 contiguous channels per thread; NCHW side writes 4 contiguous spatial positions per thread; the 90-degree turn happens in shared memory, which is untouched by DRAM. This cuts global load/store instructions 4x and widens each request, directly attacking the 68.3% long-scoreboard stall and the 72.5% DRAM utilisation gap (peers reach 82%) without changing bytes moved, dtype, or numerics.
strategy.modification_plan:
1. In gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel, replace the 4 scalar global loads of the NHWC input per thread with ONE float4 load covering 4 consecutive channels (NHWC is contiguous in C, C=256 so C%4==0 always), and replace the 4 scalar global stores/residual loads with ONE float4 store + ONE float4 residual load covering 4 consecutive spatial positions (NCHW is contiguous in P). Numerics unchanged: silu(v*scale+shift)+res is applied element-wise on the float4 lanes.
2. Same mechanism in nchw2nhwc_kernel: float4 load along P (NCHW), float4 store along C (NHWC); no scalar path remains in the vector kernel.
3. Tile/block geometry for the new K5v: tile 64 channels x 64 spatial positions, block 256 threads (32,8). Shared memory float tile[64][68] (pad 4 floats per row) = 17.4 KB/block -> under the 227 KB per-block limit and allows >=8 concurrent blocks/SM (registers ~32, occupancy stays >=8 blocks). Each thread performs 4 float4 loads and 4 float4 stores (64*64/4 = 1024 float4 per phase / 256 threads = 4).
4. Load phase (K5v): p = p0 + (tid/16), c4 = tid%16; read float4 at in[((n*P)+p)*C + c0 + 4*c4]; apply scale/shift + SiLU per lane using scale[n*C+c] broadcast from a per-block __shared__ float sc[64], sh[64] preloaded once (64 threads load them coalesced); store the 4 results as scalars tile[c][p] (stride 68). Repeat 4 times with p += 16.
5. Store phase: __syncthreads(); c = c0 + (tid/16), p4 = tid%16; read tile[c][p0+4*p4 .. +3] (contiguous in shared memory, one float4 load) -> add float4 residual res[n*C*P + c*P + p] -> one float4 store to out[same index]. Repeat 4 times with c += 16.
6. Alignment/tail guard (critical for the awkward 131x131 shape): the NCHW float4 requires (P % 4 == 0) so that c*P keeps 16 B alignment. In the host wrapper, dispatch to the vectorized kernels only when (P % 4 == 0); otherwise launch the EXISTING scalar nchw2nhwc_kernel / gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel unchanged. P=8192/4096/65536 take the fast path; P=17161 keeps today's code and today's timing bit-for-bit.
7. Handle the P-tail inside the vector path with a `p0 + 63 < P` fast branch and a masked slow branch that still uses float4 (P%4==0 guarantees whole float4 groups; only whole-group masking is needed). C tail needs no mask (C=256, multiple of 64).
8. Keep the scale/shift preload in shared memory so the per-thread affine constants are read once per block instead of once per element (removes the redundant scalar scale/shift global loads currently issued per tile column).
9. Do not touch stats_partial_kernel, stats_finalize_kernel, gn_silu_nhwc_kernel, the at::conv2d calls, weight channels-last conversion, or the fallback path. Kernel launch count per forward stays 11.
10. Validate: compare against F.conv2d/group_norm/silu reference on all four shapes; assert max_atol < 0.0027 (tightest tolerance) and confirm the 131x131 shape hits the scalar fallback (add a debug counter in a test build only).
strategy.evidence: gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel: gpu__time_duration.avg = 129216 ns (largest custom kernel; K1 68768, K4 67520, stats 2x42112), gpu__dram_throughput = 72.54% vs 82.11% (gn_silu_nhwc, float4) and 81.0% (K1) — measured 1.4795 TB/s against the ~2.04 TB/s these kernels achieve at 100%, i.e. ~99 us roofline for its 201 MB. long_scoreboard stall = 68.28% of 29.1 warp-cycles/issue, l1tex hit 13.52%, l1tex throughput only 22.23% — root cause: all three streams use 4-byte scalar accesses (128 B/warp request), so the kernel issues 4x the memory instructions of the float4 K4 and cannot cover DRAM latency. Refutation of 'occupancy-limited': achieved occupancy 91.04% and warps_active 91.22% are the highest of any kernel here, so more warps cannot be the fix. Refutation of 'shared-memory/bank-conflict bound': short_scoreboard is only 3.50% and smem spilling requests are 0, so the smem transpose is not the stall.

Anti-regression constraints: DRAM bytes moved per forward must NOT increase (same 603 MB); launches per forward stay 11; the 1x256x131x131 shape (P%4!=0) must take the untouched scalar path and change by <=1%; no shape may regress >2%; max_atol must stay under each workload tolerance (0.0027-0.003); registers/thread <=40 so occupancy stays >=8 blocks/SM.

strategy.bottleneck: [latency/serialization of complementary-bound stages] Hottest non-removable segment is the composite cuDNN TF32 fprop mainloop (~804us of the 1179us forward, ~0.33 TB/s DRAM = ~16% of achievable) executed strictly serially with the DRAM-bound GN/SiLU/transpose chain (375us at 72-82% DRAM but only 15-50% SM). Compute-bound and bandwidth-bound work never coexist, so ~375us of memory time is fully exposed.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Per-sample stream pipelining: GroupNorm statistics are per (n,group) and conv/residual are per-sample, so the block decomposes EXACTLY along batch. Split N into chunks, run each chunk's full 9-kernel sequence on one of two side CUDA streams, so chunk i's cuDNN conv (SM/tensor-core bound, 84% of DRAM idle) overlaps chunk i-1's stats/gn_silu/transpose kernels (80%+ DRAM, <50% SM). Vendor conv mainloop is kept untouched; only scheduling changes.
strategy.modification_plan:
1) EXACT DECOMPOSITION (in fused_res_block, before any launch): compute `int nchunks = (N >= 4 && (size_t)N*C*P*4ull >= (32u<<20)) ? std::min(4, N) : 1; int cs = (N + nchunks - 1)/nchunks; nchunks = (N + cs - 1)/cs;`. If nchunks==1 execute today's code path verbatim (bit-identical kernel sequence, single stream) — this is the mandatory fallback for the N=1 (1x256x131x131) and N=2 (2x256x64x64) shapes.
2) EXACT STREAM PLUMBING: hoist `auto w1c = w1.contiguous(ChannelsLast); auto w2c = w2.contiguous(ChannelsLast); at::Tensor out = at::empty({N,C,H,W}, opts);` to before the loop on the current stream. Grab `auto s0 = at::cuda::getStreamFromPool(); auto s1 = at::cuda::getStreamFromPool();`. Record `at::cuda::CUDAEvent start; start.record(main);` then `start.block(s0); start.block(s1);`. Loop `for (c=0;c<nchunks;++c){ auto st = (c&1)? s1 : s0; at::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard g(st); ... }` and inside the guard call `at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()` so every existing kernel launch and `at::conv2d` lands on `st` unmodified. After the loop: `for each side stream: CUDAEvent e; e.record(st); e.block(main);`.
3) PER-CHUNK POINTER MATH: for chunk offset `n0` and length `nc`, pass `xc.data_ptr<float>() + (size_t)n0*C*P` and `out.data_ptr<float>() + (size_t)n0*C*P` to K1/K5 with N replaced by `nc` (grids become dim3((P+31)/32, C/32, nc)); build the conv input view as `xl_c = xl.narrow(0, 0, nc)` where xl is allocated per chunk with shape {nc,C,H,W} ChannelsLast (narrow along batch preserves channels_last strides).
4) ALLOCATOR SAFETY: allocate all per-chunk intermediates (xl, y1, y1s, y2, partial, scale/shift) INSIDE the stream guard so the caching allocator tags them to `st`. For the cross-stream tensors allocated on the main stream (xc, w1c, w2c, out) call `t.record_stream(st)` once per side stream to prevent premature reuse.
5) STATS SCOPE: compute_scale_shift is already per-sample; call it with N=nc and the chunk base pointer. inv_count and the (n,g) block mapping are unchanged, so numerics are bit-identical to the unchunked path (no cross-sample reduction exists).
6) KEEP THE VENDOR MAINLOOP: do not touch at::conv2d, TF32, or the round-1 cudnn benchmark autotune; per-chunk conv shapes are constant across iterations so the benchmark cache is hit once and reused.
7) CHUNK-SIZE GUARD: require each chunk's conv GEMM to keep the GPU busy — assert `nc*P/64*2 >= 256` CTAs (mid shape: nc=2 -> 512 CTAs); if not, reduce nchunks to 2 or 1.
8) BONUS (not the mechanism): per-chunk working set is 16.7MB at the mid shape, so the stats->K4 and stats->K5 re-reads of the same chunk may now hit L2; do not restructure anything else to chase this.
9) VALIDATION: run all four shapes; confirm nsys shows sm90_xmma fprop ranges overlapping stats_partial/gn_silu ranges, confirm max_atol under each workload tolerance, and confirm the N<4 shapes emit exactly 11 launches on the default stream.
strategy.evidence: Convs = 804us/1179us (nsys: 24 fprop launches/12 forwards) moving only 134MB -> ~0.33 TB/s = ~16% of the 2.04 TB/s these kernels actually achieve; meanwhile stats_partial gpu__dram_throughput=80.2% with sm__throughput=15.8%, gn_silu_nhwc 82.4% DRAM / 46.3% SM, nchw2nhwc 81.3% DRAM / 50.6% SM, stats_finalize 0.28 waves/SM. Root cause: strictly serial chaining of a tensor-core-bound mainloop and a DRAM-bound epilogue chain leaves each unit idle in turn; GroupNorm is per-(n,g) so the chain is exactly separable by batch. Refutation of the 'K5 is the bottleneck, vectorize it' alternative: gn_silu_res_nchw moves 201MB, roofline 99us vs 128.2us measured = only 29us (2.5% of the forward) of slack, and history round 3 (mem_vectorize) measured 1.549 < round 1's 1.566; the hideable memory time is 375us, an order of magnitude larger.

(2) GPU-level gpu__dram_throughput during the conv windows rises from ~16% toward >=40%; stats_finalize's 2x13us latency-bound launches become fully hidden. Per-launch custom-kernel durations may rise <=15% from SM contention — acceptable only if total time falls. strategy.bottleneck: [latency-bound reduction inside the hottest custom composite] The GroupNorm segment (stats_partial 2x42.2us + stats_finalize 2x13.2us + apply kernels 67.2us/129.9us) is 307us of the 375us custom-kernel time. Its reduction is split across two launches through a 2MB partial buffer; stats_finalize does no bandwidth work (DRAM 7.89%, 0.28 waves/SM, 25.6% occupancy) and is 87% uncoalesced-sector bound, costing ~26us per forward almost independently of shape.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: atomic_privatize: privatize the group reduction inside stats_partial. Each block already holds all 256 channels, so reduce the 8 lanes of each group in-register (__shfl_down width 8) and atomicAdd 32 (sum,sumsq) pairs into a tiny [N][G][2] accumulator, then let the last arriving block per image (atomic counter + __threadfence) emit scale/shift. This deletes the 2MB partial round-trip, the 87%-excessive-sector strided loads and both latency-bound stats_finalize launches, which metrics show are pure launch/latency cost, not bandwidth.
strategy.modification_plan:
Checklist (all inside compute_scale_shift + stats kernel; K1/K4/K5/conv untouched):
1. Delete the `partial` tensor `at::empty({2, N*nchunks*C})` and the entire `stats_finalize_kernel` launch. Allocate ONE zeroed scratch for BOTH norms at the top of fused_res_block: `auto acc = at::zeros({2, N*G*2 + N}, opts)` reinterpreted as {float acc[N][G][2]; float ctr[N];} per norm (ctr read as int*). This is one tiny memset for the whole forward, so launches/forward go 11 -> 10 while removing 2x13.2us kernels.
2. Rename stats_partial_kernel -> stats_atomic_kernel(in, acc, ctr, scale, shift, gamma, beta, P, C, chunk, nchunks, G, CPG, inv_count, eps). Keep the existing accumulation loop byte-for-byte (`ptr += C`, `__ldg`) - it is already 80.8% DRAM and coalesced; only the epilogue changes.
3. In-register group reduction (replaces the global partial write): with c = threadIdx.x, CPG = C/G = 8 contiguous lanes per group, do
   `#pragma unroll for (int off = CPG>>1; off; off >>= 1) { s += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffff, s, off, CPG); q += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffff, q, off, CPG); }`
   then `if ((c & (CPG-1)) == 0) { int g = c / CPG; atomicAdd(&acc[((n*G)+g)*2+0], s); atomicAdd(&acc[((n*G)+g)*2+1], q); }`. Generic guard: if CPG is not a power of two or CPG > 32, fall back to a 256-float shared-memory segmented reduction (never taken for C=256,G=32).
4. Last-block finalize (removes the second launch): `__threadfence(); __shared__ int isLast; if (threadIdx.x==0) isLast = (atomicAdd(&ctr_i[n],1) == nchunks-1); __syncthreads(); if (isLast) { int g = c / CPG; float sm = acc[(n*G+g)*2+0]*inv_count; float v = acc[(n*G+g)*2+1]*inv_count - sm*sm; v = v<0.f?0.f:v; float r = rsqrtf(v+eps); float gm = gamma?gamma[c]:1.f, bt = beta?beta[c]:0.f; scale[n*C+c] = r*gm; shift[n*C+c] = bt - sm*r*gm; }` - one fully coalesced 256-float store pair per (n) instead of the 458752 excessive sectors the old finalize generated.
